Subject: April invoice: large oscillation in token counts across aggregation windows

Hi Connor —

We just received the April invoice and noticed a ~42% swing in billed tokens for our streaming endpoints compared to March. The spike looks correlated with multiple short bursts (many <300-token calls) in the 04/08–04/12 window.

Attached is a payload export and a screenshot from our monitoring that shows the bucketing change we think exposed a double-count. Can you confirm whether Redwood changed any aggregation/windowing rules or sampling parameters in early April? We need the raw per-request metering logs and an explanation to share with our finance team; until resolved we are asking our AP team to hold payment for the disputed amount.

Attachments: pulse_usage_export_Q1.csv, metering_screenshot_agg_windows.png

Thanks,

Subject: Re: April invoice: large oscillation in token counts across aggregation windows

Connor / team / Paul —

Preliminary findings from the metering export (attached):
- We ran a per-request export for the period requested and compared aggregation window boundaries.
- There was a configuration change on 2027-04-07 at 02:04 UTC that tightened the streaming aggregation cutoff from 5s to 1s for high-concurrency routes (intent was to reduce latency for interactive flows).
- That change inadvertently increased event granularity for short bursts, which in some payload patterns can look like multiple distinct requests and therefore increased the billed token count for calls that previously were grouped.

Evidence we are attaching: per_request_export_20270325_20270420.csv (excerpt), a short diagram of before/after bucket boundaries, and a proposed credit calculation.

Proposed remediation & timeline:
1) Apply an aggregation guard that collapses sub-1s adjacent events from the same connection when session metadata matches (deploy within 48 hours).
2) Recompute the April billed tokens for PulseAI using the guard and produce an adjusted invoice & credit note (target: 2027-05-05).
3) Offer a one-time credit equal to the delta for the disputed window; if you prefer, we can amortize as a discount across the May invoice.

If you want an immediate dampening we can also apply a one-off retrospective adjustment for that window while we ship the guard.

Attachments: proposed_credit_calc.xlsx, per_request_export_excerpt.csv

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20 minute call if you want to walk through the evidence.

—Ben Carter
Billing Operations Lead — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Connor / Ben —

Thanks for the quick analysis, Ben. The change on 04-07 lines up with our internal incident spike. We appreciate the remediation plan. A few asks before we lift payment hold:
1) Please provide the full per-request export (not an excerpt) in CSV with request_id, timestamp, route, token_in, token_out, and connection_id.
2) Confirm whether the proposed guard will be retroactive for billing only (i.e., we want the credit but do not want the runtime change to impact our production latency expectations unless we opt in).
3) Send a short reconciliation CSV formatted for our AP system (columns: invoice_line_item, original_amount, adjusted_amount, credit_reference).

If those items are delivered by EOD Thursday (05/05) and the credit calculation matches our independent tally, we will lift the payment hold and process the adjusted invoice. Otherwise our AP will keep the hold.

Paul
